newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's H-shares take hit as market dives on dlr woes.
newsitem.headline: HK's H-shares take hit as market dives on dlr woes.

text.p: H-shares were hard hit on Tuesday, with a recent rally making them particularly vulnerable to Hong Kong's broad market triggered by fears of a speculative attack on the Hong Kong dollar and a surge in interbank rates.
"The fall on H-shares is steeper than the Hang Seng as they are more speculative and have been risen so much lately," said Franco Tong, institutional sales manager at New China Hong Kong.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index, or H-share index, was down 7.54 percent in mid-afternoon, compared to the blue chip Hang Seng Index's 4.48 percent decline.
Tong said the immediate market trend would depend on the performance of the local currency but some investors were waiting to buy on dips.
Hong Kong overnight rates stablilised at around 8.00 to 11.00 percent at midday against a high of 18.00/20.00 percent reached in early trade on Tuesday.
The Hong Kong dollar weakened to HK$7.7430/40 against the U.S. dollar from a local opening level of HK$7.7400/10.
Guangdong Kelon fell HK$1.20 to HK$10.00 and Shanghai Hai Xing Shipping fell HK$0.60 to HK$6.25.
Yizheng Chemical was the only gainer in the sector and rose HK$0.05 to HK$3.85.
